newsitem.title: USA: Clinton accuser sees victory in court case.
newsitem.headline: Clinton accuser sees victory in court case.

text.p: A lawyer for Paula Jones predicted on Friday she would win her Supreme Court case to get a lower court hearing on her charges that President Bill Clinton sexually harassed her nearly six years ago.
The high court plans to hear arguments on Monday by the former Arkansas state worker's lawyers who are trying to have her case heard while Clinton is in office.

Joseph Cammarata said on "Fox Morning News" he believed his client would win the Supreme Court case. "I think so," he said, when asked if his client would get a high court go-ahead for a lower court to hear her complaint.
Jones, 30, wants $700,000 in damages from Clinton who she says exposed himself in a hotel room with her on May 8, 1991 when he was Arkansas governor and she was a state worker.

"Paula Jones is a credible person, " Cammarata said. "She has some compelling evidence in support of her position. What she wants most of all is an opportunity to be heard, an opportunity to present her case, not on some political soapbox but in a forum where truth, in fact, can be tried and she is confident that if given her day in court her good name and reputation will be restored," he added.
Her lawyers filed their case against Clinton in 1994. The president has denied the charges against him.

Clinton's lawyer, Robert Bennett, argues that the case should not be heard until Clinton leaves office as it would set a bad precedent that would leave future presidents open to distracting lawsuits whether the charges have merit or not.

Asked by a reporter on Friday if the Supreme Court hearing would be an unwelcome distraction as he begins his second term, Clinton said: "I don't have any control over what anyone else does, I can only control what I do."
"It's not going to cause me any difficulty because I'm going to do my job here," he said.

In the television interview, Cammarata repeated Jones' claim that she "can identify distinguishing characteristics in Bill Clinton's genital area that became obvious to her because of his indecent exposure and solicitation of sex."

Cammarata also said he and Clinton's lawyer came close to settling the case in private negotiations before she filed her lawsuit "but the White House spin doctors blew it up" through leaks and claims that she did not have a case against Clinton.
